title: London
summary:
This document is a comprehensive encyclopedia article about London, the capital of England and the United Kingdom. It begins with an overview of London's significance as a global city, its population, geography on the River Thames, and its influence on world finance, culture, education, and tourism. The article then explores the etymology of the name "London," tracing it back to the Roman-era Londinium and Celtic origins.

A substantial history section chronicles London's development from prehistoric settlements through Roman occupation, Anglo-Saxon and Viking periods, the Middle Ages, the early modern era (including the Reformation, English Civil War, Great Plague, and Great Fire), and late modern times (covering the Industrial Revolution, World Wars, post-war immigration, and modern developments like the 7/7 bombings and the creation of the Greater London Authority).

The article details London's administrative structure, including the two-tier governance system of the Greater London Authority and 33 local authorities, as well as national government presence. The geography section covers the city's scope, topography along the Thames, temperate climate, distinct areas such as the West End and East End, architectural styles spanning from Tudor to modern skyscrapers, and rich natural history.

Further sections address London's diverse demographics (ethnic composition, religious groups, and accents including Cockney and Multicultural London English), its robust economy centered on finance, media, technology, and tourism, and its extensive transport network comprising airports, the London Underground, rail systems, buses, and river services. The article also covers London's world-renowned educational institutions, vibrant cultural scene including West End theatre, museums, and music, its abundant parks and green spaces, and its major sporting venues and events, including having hosted the Summer Olympics three times.
